correctness.rationale: An exact 24-degree monic polynomial P=Phi_70 is reconstructed from cyclotomic factorization. For j=0..53 the linear remainder functional 2[R_j]_{19}+[R_j]_{20}+2[R_j]_{21}+[R_j]_{22}+[R_j]_{23} is identically zero except at j=19..34, where its sixteen integer weights are all positive (2,1,2,1,1,1,2,3,3,2,1,1,1,2,1,2); the standalone standard-library verifier recomputes every coefficient. For any nonnegative real polynomial of degree <=53 divisible by P, linearity and positivity kill all those sixteen coefficients. It is A+X^35 B with degrees <=18, and X^35=-1 modulo P forces P|(A-B); degree <24 forces A=B. This covers every real coefficient vector, not merely enumerated integer examples. The supplied 16-support W has exact quotient P*Q, diameter 54 and unequal coefficients at indices 0 and 35, so it is not an antipodal-binomial multiple. Limits: only index 70; nothing claimed for other N or full degree-54 cone.

originality.rationale: The focal source gives sharp minimum diameter 35 and equality classification, whereas the claim determines all positive multiples through diameter 53 and the first non-antipodal degree 54. Source 2012 provides a dual-certificate method for minimum degree but its inspected theorem/examples do not state this longer exact stability interval. The 2020/2025 weight classification includes order-70 minimal vanishing sums and can encompass the exhibited 16-term witness type, so novelty is not assigned to the witness type; it does not itself supply the all-weights nonnegative-real coefficient-cone rigidity claimed here. The exact decimal bounds 53 and 54, the positive coefficient certificate, and the full implication comparison were not found in the performed search. Residual risk is specific: unindexed exact diameter tables, source Section 5 material not fully available in this session, and known minimal-sum classifications might be combined with further arguments. No claim of global uniqueness is made.

value.rationale: The source sharp minimum-D theorem leaves a natural next question: how long does the entire nonnegative cone remain generated solely by antipodal pairs? At the small three-prime order N=70=2*5*7, the new exact answer is every diameter <=53 (19 possible diameters from 35 through 53) and the first failure 54. This is not a mere first extra degree; its first non-antipodal 16-term relation at 54 precedes the obvious 5-cycle at 56, demonstrating a genuine structural transition. The exact cone classification for all real nonnegative coefficient vectors is a reusable extremal datum for vanishing root sums. Its limitation to a natural order with two odd prime factors >=5 and the non-general nature of the result are explicitly disclosed.
